clauses.reason: Terminated by its own terms at the close of Monday, December 31, 1934, the second of the two afternoons on which it closes the offices and excuses employees ('at 1 P.M. on Monday, December 24, 1934, and at 1 P.M. on Monday, December 31, 1934'). The dossier holds no own-terms record for this order, so the end cites the order's complete registered text, which contains the stated days.

research_rationale:
Text and identity: read in full in the registered American Presidency Project transcription (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts; grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md (working-text paragraph), done 2026-10-28: the page record with the same sha256 in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl (an archived capture whose archive and WARC location are recorded) has a heading naming this order number, a date and subject agreeing with the held text, and a text_sha256 equal to the held file's. Clauses are quoted from that registered file, not from the clause-drafts copy. EO 6920 (December 13, 1934, Franklin D. Roosevelt), read in full. It closes the executive departments, independent establishments and other government agencies in the District of Columbia, including the Government Printing Office and the Navy Yard and stations, 'at 1 P.M. on Monday, December 24, 1934' and 'at 1 P.M. on Monday, December 31, 1934', and excuses federal employees in the District and in the field service from duty at those hours, except those excluded by their agency heads for special public reasons or whose absence would conflict with existing law. Identity: number, date and subject agree across the APP page record and the census register; the A, B and C orders of the same number are different instruments. First end: by its own terms at the close of 1934-12-31, the second and last day it governs (the December 24 part was spent at the close of that day). Searches made on 2026-10-28: census register titles and the WPA 1944 list for December 1934 closings, and a citation search of every held order text for 'No. 6920' and 'Order 6920'; the hits are EO 6920-A, 6920-B and 6920-C, which concern other subjects and do not name this order. The machine USC and eCFR searches (complete, 0 hits) exclude a current-law reference; the OFR catalog search starts in 1937 and is not relied on alone.
